chapters.title: The Lantern Comes Home
lines: The Lantern came into Brinehold on a grey morning, her sails furled and her deck slick with rain.
Mira Voss stood at the bow with the brass compass in her fist. She was the captain of the Night Watch now, though the title still sat on her shoulders like a borrowed coat.
The harbourmaster, a thin man named Pell, met her at the quay. "Captain Voss," he said, and glanced at her face. "You have your mother's eyes."
Mira had heard that before. Her eyes were grey, the colour of the sea before a storm, and she did not know whether the comparison was a kindness or a warning.
Behind the town, the lighthouse stood dark against the clouds. Its lens had been cracked for three years, and no ship had trusted the coast since.
"Mira!" A red-haired man pushed through the crowd. Kael Voss wiped soot from his hands and grinned. "You stayed away long enough."

chapters.title: The Forge on the Salt Road
lines: Kael's forge sat at the end of the Salt Road, where the cobbles gave way to packed sand. The sign above the door was a horseshoe, and the heat rolled out of it like breath.
"You are still a blacksmith," Mira said.
"Someone has to shoe the horses you keep drowning," Kael said. He was her brother, and he had the same stubborn jaw as their mother.
"Show me your hand," Mira said. Kael sighed and turned his left palm up. The old burn scar ran from his thumb to his wrist, pale against his skin.
"It was the forge," he said. "Not the war."
Mira looked at the scar and then at the rows of iron hooks on the wall. "The Salt Road is where the Night Watch was betrayed," she said.
Kael's hammer stopped. "I know."

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Light
lines: The lighthouse keeper was named Orin Hale. He was older than the tower itself, or so the fishermen said, and he had lost two fingers to a cold winter.
"Three years," Orin said, tapping the cracked lens. "Three years since the light went wrong."
Mira climbed the spiral stair behind him. The lens filled the whole room, a shattered eye of glass and brass.
"The Night Watch paid for the repair," she said.
"The Night Watch paid for a lot of things," Orin said. "The bell rings only for the drowned, Captain. Remember that."
Below them, the sea moved like a slow animal.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Green Coat
lines: Sera Dunne found Mira on the Salt Road at dusk. She wore a green coat that had been mended at both elbows, and she carried a roll of tide charts under one arm.
"The smuggler," Mira said.
"The trader," Sera corrected. "Smuggling is just trade with worse paperwork."
They walked together past the shuttered shops. Sera unrolled a chart and showed Mira the channels that ran between the sandbars.
"These will take you to the Drowned Abbey," Sera said. "If you have the nerve."
Mira studied the chart. "Why would I go there?"
"Because the compass in your pocket is pointing east," Sera said. "And because your mother left something behind."

chapters.title: The Betrayal
lines: The Night Watch had been betrayed at the Salt Road on the night of the storm. Eight men had died, and the ship that was meant to meet them had never come.
Mira read the old report by candlelight. A witness said the traitor wore a grey cloak and spoke with a Brinehold accent.
"Grey cloak," Kael said. "Half the town owns one."
"The witness also said the traitor knew the tide charts," Mira said.
Kael put down his hammer. "Then ask Sera."
Mira closed the report. "I intend to."

chapters.title: The Brass Compass
lines: In the ashes of Kael's forge, Mira found a brass compass. It was small enough to hide in a fist, and the needle did not point north.
The needle pointed east, toward the Drowned Abbey.
Kael came in from the yard and saw the compass in her hand. "That was Mother's," he said quietly.
"She was a lighthouse keeper," Mira said. "Not a sailor."
"She was both," Kael said.
The compass clicked once, as if it had heard him.

chapters.title: The Tide Bell
lines: The storm struck Brinehold at midnight. Rain came sideways off the sea, and the windows of the Salt Road shook in their frames.
Mira stood on the quay with the brass compass in her hand. The needle spun once and then held east.
Out in the harbour, the tide bell began to ring. It rang three times, slow and flat, and every fisherman on the quay crossed himself.
Orin had said the bell rings only for the drowned. No one had drowned that night.
No one they knew of.

chapters.title: What Kael Sold
lines: Kael confessed at dawn. He had sold the lighthouse lens to pay a debt, and the debt had been called in by men from the Salt Road.
"I did not sell the Night Watch," he said. "Only the light."
Mira wanted to hit him. Instead she asked, "Who bought it?"
"A woman in a green coat," Kael said. "She paid in silver and asked no questions."
The forge was cold. The scar on Kael's left palm looked pale in the morning light.
Mira put the compass on the anvil between them. "You should have told me."
"I know," Kael said.

chapters.title: The Drowned Abbey
lines: The Drowned Abbey stood in the shallows east of Brinehold, its roof open to the rain. The tide charts had been right: a channel ran between the sandbars, deep enough for a small boat.
Mira lit a lantern and stepped into the nave. Water covered the floor to her ankles, and the stone saints watched from their niches with broken faces.
A woman's voice came through the wall. It was her mother's voice, or the memory of it.
"Mira," the voice said. "You came back."
Her mother had been a lighthouse keeper before her. She had also kept a secret.
Mira pressed her palm to the stone. "Who are you?" she asked.
The voice did not answer.

chapters.title: The Traitor
lines: Sera Dunne was waiting at the abbey door, still wearing her green coat. The tide charts were gone. In their place she held a long knife.
"It was you," Mira said. "You betrayed the Night Watch."
"I warned them about the storm," Sera said. "They chose not to listen."
"You sold the lighthouse lens."
"Kael sold the lens. I bought it."
Sera had stolen the light, and the Night Watch had paid for it with eight lives. The knife did not shake in her hand.

chapters.title: The Captain in the Water
lines: Mira looked into the still water of the abbey. Her grey eyes looked back at her, and for the first time she did not see her mother in them.
She saw a captain.
Kael waited in the boat with the lantern. "I am sorry," he said.
"I know," Mira said. She climbed in and took the oars. "You are still my brother."
Behind them, the abbey sank back into the tide. The brass compass in Mira's pocket clicked once, and the needle turned north.

chapters.title: North
lines: The Lantern sailed at dawn. The lighthouse lens was still missing, and the tower stayed dark, but the harbour opened before them like a hand.
Orin stood on the quay with his two remaining fingers raised in farewell.
"The bell will ring again," he called. "It always does."
Mira raised the brass compass. The needle held north.
Who had her mother been? The question followed the ship out of Brinehold, and Mira did not have an answer.
Somewhere under the water, the tide bell rang once.
